scope: shape, proportions, hierarchy, attachment, and facial placement; existing game palette and lighting remain authoritative
observations: The current rendered head, torso, limbs, hands, legs, and feet share one SDF surface.
The shared surface visibly blends unrelated colors across the face and torso.
The current solid hair ellipsoid covers most of the forehead and side silhouette.
The current feet and legs lose their independent silhouettes in front and side views.
inferences: Rear head and hair-shell shape are authored symmetrically because no dedicated rear reference was supplied.
The existing game uses -Z as character forward, so the written +Z convention is adapted without changing gameplay orientation.

componentTree.surface: thin scalp cap plus three broad fringe masses

attachmentContract.limbs: Every lower segment is parented to its upper-segment pivot; every hand/foot is parented to its lower-segment pivot.
attachmentContract.face: All face anchors are children of FaceAnchor and are projected onto one analytic head ellipsoid before receiving a shallow normal offset.
attachmentContract.hair: Hair is an independent Head child and never participates in the skin SDF.
attachmentContract.clothing: Outfit, hat, scarf, pants, shoes, and held equipment remain separate CreatureOutfit geometry driven by pose anchors.

materials.rule: one explicit palette color; no cross-part distance blending

acceptance: No visible human body is rendered by CreatureSdfShell.
Only the two same-material head volumes share an SDF blend domain.
Eyes and blush anchors are mathematically mirrored.
Nose and mouth remain centered on X=0.
Head, torso, arms, hands, legs, feet, hair, and outfit retain independent semantic nodes and materials.
Bare front, three-quarter, and side captures preserve distinct hands, legs, and feet.
